about: Hand-set flight directions for upcoming launches whose direction Launch Library 2 does not give. Keyed by LL2 launch id. Each entry gives either azimuthDeg, or inclinationDeg with heading 'northeast', 'southeast' or 'both' (both draws the two possible paths). profile is optional (default falcon9-leo). How to find a direction, with URLs: reference/topics/cape-launch-azimuths-and-inclinations.md, section 'Runbook: finding the direction of an upcoming launch'. Remove an entry after the launch, or keep it as a record; it only applies to that launch id.

3b430f81-0ff1-4d85-8a1a-cef0de326198.source: Heading set to southeast on 2026-10-18 from Coast Guard Broadcast Notice to Mariners CGD-SE BNM 9080-26, 'Launch Hazard Area, Mission: BANDWAGON-5', seen by Ben on the NAVCEN chart viewer (https://navcen.uscg.gov/chart, iPhone screenshot 2026-10-18 07:04 local). Windows 1030Z to 1213Z each day, 19 to 25 OCT 26. The polygon is east of the Bahamas; a point on it (25.42 N 74.355 W, read from the map cursor, so approximate) is about 708 km from SLC-40 on bearing 118, near the southeast track (126.4) and far from the northeast one (53.6). The polygon coordinates were not read as text. The drone ship had not yet sailed: orbitalradar fleet hub showed ASOG at Port Canaveral at 06:53 local on 2026-10-18 (Ben's screenshot); LL2 still gave ASOG, 600 km (record last_updated 2026-10-17T17:51:39Z, read 2026-10-18). Earlier note: LL2 says 'mid-inclination orbit' (read 2026-10-15). SpaceNews reports SpaceX said Bandwagon missions go to inclinations of about 45 degrees (https://spacenews.com/spacex-to-offer-mid-inclination-smallsat-rideshare-launches/, read 2026-10-15); Bandwagon 3 went to 45 degrees (orbitcodex.com, secondary). Conflict: Wikipedia's October to December 2026 launch list gives SSO; the mission name and LL2 do not support that. Expected drone ship station: off the Carolinas about 31.7 N 75.5 W for northeast, near the Bahamas about 25.3 N 75.8 W for southeast; check after it sails.
